Boeing upgraded, Enphase downgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.

Top 5 Upgrades:

Langenberg upgraded Boeing (BA) with a $250 price target following the earnings report. The firm sees "plenty of good news in the quarter" despite Boeing's delay in commercial airplane production increases for the 737 and 787.

BNP Paribas upgraded Pentair (PNR) to Neutral from Underperform with a $65 price target. The firm believes the company has sufficiently reset expectations, creating a more balanced risk/reward at current share levels.

Jefferies upgraded Chemed (CHE) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $620, up from $520. The firm expects the shares to "gradually re-rate" toward 15-times EBITDA as the company "returns to a stable earnings growth trajectory."

Freedom Broker upgraded Piedmont Realty Trust (PDM) to Buy from Hold with an unchanged price target of $11. The company's Q3 results reflected continued strength in its operating fundamentals, the firm tells investors in a research note

Scotiabank upgraded Sun Life Financial (SLF) to Outperform from Sector Perform with a price target of C$122, up from C$118. The lifecos are expected to deliver another decent quarter in Q3 with mid-to-high single-digit core EPS gains, supported by a stable macro backdrop, constructive markets, and solid access to capital that allows for active share buybacks, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Top 5 Downgrades:

Roth Capital downgraded Enphase Energy (ENPH) to Neutral from Buy with a price target of $30, down from $55. The company delivered a weak set of Q3 earnings and a meaningful miss on Q4 guidance, the firm tells investors in a research note. Oppenheimer also downgraded Enphase Energy to Perform from Outperform after the company missed Q3 Street expectations while guiding well below consensus and indicating baseline demand of about $200M revenue/quarter for its core businesses.

JPMorgan downgraded Xylem (XYL) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $90, down from $118. The company's Q3 results came in slightly below expectations and fiscal 2026 guidance was lowered on slower revenue conversion in metering and water solutions project timing, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Piper Sandler downgraded F5 (FFIV) to Neutral from Overweight with an unchanged price target of $461 following the fiscal Q4 report. Piper believes dynamics remain in F5's favor, but the shares are fairly priced at this level.

Stifel downgraded Whirlpool (WHR) to Sell from Hold with a price target of $20, down from $30, after its Q3 earnings miss and guidance cut. The company's challenges are likely to accelerate as Whirlpool is losing market share in the key U.S. market, the firm tells investors in a research note.

Jefferies downgraded Simply Good Foods (SMPL) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $11, down from $15. The firm believes fiscal 2027 is positioned to be an "even tougher year" for Simply.

Salesforce will purchase 500,000 high-integrity, data-backed methane reduction credits from Mitti Labs by 2030, bringing water resilience to India's smallholder farmers.

SAN FRANCISCO and BENGALURU, India, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Deep-tech company Mitti Labs today announced a five-year carbon credit offtake agreement with Salesforce to scale Climate-smart rice farming across tens of thousands of smallholder farms in India. Coming just weeks after Mitti Labs' offtake agreement with Google, this new partnership shows the growing corporate demand for satellite-verified rice methane credits as a scalable offset solution with near-term impact.

Mitti Labs and Salesforce partner to scale water-saving rice farming practices that help reduce methane emissions

Climate-smart rice farming replaces traditional continuous irrigation with alternate irrigation, where farmers let their fields dry out during safe windows in the growing cycle. This low-cost practice shift helps the world grow more rice with less water, while abating methane emissions derived from microbe growth in oxygen-free soils. Alternate irrigation can cut methane emissions by up to 50% and water usage by up to 40%, without affecting yields.

Agriculture is responsible for 40% of all human-induced methane emissions, which are a powerful driver of climate change. Methane traps 85 times more heat than CO₂ but only stays in the atmosphere for a decade, meaning that every ton that is not emitted today delivers a fast, tangible reduction in near-term warming.

Commitments from companies like Salesforce are helping Mitti Labs scale these practices. Mitti Labs plans to scale its operations to meet this demand: by 2028, it plans to issue 2 million credits per year from its projects located in India and Southeast Asia.

"Salesforce is a founding member of the Beyond Alliance's Superpollutant Action Initiative. We know that superpollutant reduction is one of the best ways to slow near-term warming, and we are committed to directing capital toward high-impact mitigation efforts. Reducing methane emissions from rice farming is a scalable climate solution that also helps preserve water resources for future generations," said Jamila Yamani, PhD., Director of Climate & Energy at Salesforce.

Every credit delivered under the agreement will be backed by field-level evidence and satellite-verified field dry-downs. Mitti Labs' GeoAI platform, developed with support from NASA, fuses high-resolution satellite radar with field-collected ground truth to track flooding, soil moisture and crop health across individual smallholder plots. This provides credit buyers with transparent, independently verifiable proof of impact at a scale that manual monitoring is not able to match.

title: What Is Going On With Salesforce Stock?
detail:
What Is Going On With Salesforce Stock?

Shares of Salesforce (CRM) trade at 20.4 times earnings. That multiple trails the 22.6 median for S&P 500 companies, following a year where the software maker's stock fell while the S&P 500 rose. Over the last twelve months, Salesforce grew revenue 11.2%, outpacing the 8.5% median company growth rate. Buyers at this price need those earnings to come from selling software, and they need the growth from Slack and Agentforce to last. How solid are those earnings?

Most Of Salesforce's Earnings Come From Selling Software

Salesforce earned a 21.5% operating margin over the last twelve months, clearing the 18.5% median for the S&P 500. Investors also pay less for each dollar of cash flow, putting a 12.5 multiple on Salesforce's cash from operations against 15.2 for the broader market.

The profit supporting that P/E ratio presents a soft spot. Salesforce posted a 22.0% net margin over the same twelve months. With net margin sitting higher than operating margin, a portion of that profit came from outside day-to-day operations. The divergence happened in one quarter only: in fiscal Q2 2027, when net margin reached 31.1% against a 21.4% operating margin. That operating margin was also down from the 22.8% reported in fiscal Q2 2026.

Salesforce's Growth Has More Than Halved Since 2022

Current pricing appears to assume Salesforce will maintain its current growth rate rather than returning to the pace of a few years ago. Revenue expanded 24.6% in the twelve months to July 2022, compared with 11.2% over the last twelve months. By the end of September 2026, investors paid 4.3 times Salesforce's sales. Stretching back to the end of 2016, investors paid less at just two of the preceding 39 quarter ends.

The last twelve months still proved better than the prior two years. Revenue climbed 10.3% in the twelve months to July 2024 and 8.3% in the twelve months to July 2025. The latest quarter slowed down, however, with revenue up 10.8% in fiscal Q2 2027 against 13.3% in fiscal Q1. Across fiscal 2026, Salesforce's two largest business units, which the company now names Agentforce Service and Agentforce Sales, grew 8.4% and 8.5%.

Is Salesforce Lifting Growth With Slack And Agentforce?

So far, Salesforce has lifted growth in one business. The unit housing Slack and the Agentforce 360 Platform posted 22.6% growth in fiscal 2026, accelerating from 9.6% the year before. Agentforce Marketing and Agentforce Commerce moved in the opposite direction, with growth slowing to 2.8% from 7.5%.

title: Salesforce adds AI agent testing and cost controls to Agent Fabric

Salesforce adds AI agent testing and cost controls to Agent Fabric
Salesforce’s Agent Fabric currently processes more than 1.2 billion requests each day. · Verdict · gguy/Shutterstock.com.

Salesforce has announced the addition of Agent Evals, API Evals, and enhanced cost control features to Agent Fabric, its AI agent control plane designed to oversee and govern AI agents across various systems.

The company said these updates are intended to help enterprises intervene before AI agent failures or escalating costs affect customers.

Agent Fabric currently processes more than 1.2 billion requests each day, according to Salesforce.

As organisations integrate more AI agents, the risk of unnoticed failures or increasing expenses also grows, particularly given that many issues go undetected in production environments.

The company noted that fewer than half of organisations with AI agents evaluate their agents' performance on real-world traffic, leaving potential problems unaddressed until they result in customer complaints or budget overruns.

The new Agent Evals capability automatically creates and runs tests before and during agent deployment, assessing agents, large language models (LLMs), and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers against set quality benchmarks.

When these benchmarks are not met, the system can trigger interventions, such as activating an Agent Kill Switch, according to company policy.

API Evals provides automated testing of APIs relied upon by agents, aiming to identify any breaking changes before they enter production.

Salesforce has also introduced advanced cost controls through features like the FinOps Dashboard and Model Wallet.

These tools are designed to provide a consolidated view of AI spending, enforce strict usage limits, and reduce token consumption by up to 75% in testing with techniques such as semantic caching and response trimming.

Salesforce MuleSoft and Agent Fabric senior vice president and general manager Andrew Comstock said: "Enterprises can only scale agents as fast as they can keep them accurate and on budget. Today, spotting a wrong answer or a spending spike is one job, and stopping it is another.

"Agent Fabric unifies them, bringing evaluations, cost controls, and intervention together so teams can contain issues instantly and scale agents with confidence."

Additional enhancements include the Custom Agent Scanner, which allows for the discovery and cataloguing of agents, models, and APIs across internal or third-party environments.

Open Policies for Federated API Gateways enable policy enforcement across multiple API management systems.

Salesforce states these updates support continuous agent evaluation and governance, helping organisations maintain control as they scale up the deployment of AI agents.

Earlier this month, Salesforce agreed to acquire US cloud software company Braze in a deal valued at approximately $5.66bn.

"Salesforce adds AI agent testing and cost controls to Agent Fabric" was originally created and published by Verdict, a GlobalData owned brand.

After covering the costs of running the business, keeping 1.3 cents of every dollar it sells does not sound like much. But for Appian (APPN), a software company, it is the most in at least eight years. That figure represents its operating margin over the twelve months to June 2026. Can you guess what Appian's operating margin usually is?

How Unusual Is This For Appian?

Across the 39 twelve-month periods ending at each quarter close from December 2016 to June 2026, Appian's median operating margin was a loss of 16.7% of sales. That compares with a profit of 1.3% now.

The old best that Appian just beat was set only recently. Its previous best was 0.9% over the twelve months to September 2025, and the twelve months to June 2026 are the first to top it. This establishes a fresh break rather than a record Appian has extended quarter after quarter. With both figures sitting just above zero, what is rare at Appian is achieving any operating profit at all.

What Is Behind Appian's Record Operating Margin?

Large organizations in highly regulated industries use Appian software to build their own applications, and the company is selling more of it. In the quarter to June 2026, cloud subscription revenue rose 23%, climbing faster than the 19% rise in total revenue. Management attributed the quarter's strong new business to continued AI traction, noting that AI has ignited demand from customers who want to modernize older systems. Sales growth is nothing new at Appian. The company grew sales from a year earlier in each of the 38 quarters from the one ending March 2017 to the one ending June 2026. For most of that stretch, however, the growth arrived alongside an operating loss. The record itself rests on one quarter: Appian's operating margin was 7.0% in the quarter to September 2025.

Is The Latest Quarter Still Improving?

A twelve-month figure lags behind the newest quarter. Against a year earlier, the newest quarter did improve: Appian posted an operating loss in the quarter to June 2026 of 2.7% of sales, narrower than the 6.4% loss a year before. However, the company recorded an operating profit of 1.6% of sales in the preceding quarter, meaning the latest quarter slipped back into a loss. That single quarter still sits below the twelve-month record, so the twelve-month figure is running ahead of the newest quarter.
